s.t: Conan O’Brien was having a really bad day when Delta Spirit came to play ‘Trashcan’ on his show in 2008; hearing their sound check, he told them, changed his attitude.
s.src: Orlando Weekly: Delta Spirit (interview with Jon Jameson)
s.q: He came and told us later that he was having a really bad day, and then he heard us playing during our sound check and it, like, changed his attitude.” It’s easy to understand why. The song they chose for the occasion, “Trashcan,”

s.t: It grew from a jam by Delta Spirit’s Kelly Winrich and Matthew Vasquez plus a drumming friend; Winrich suspects that’s why it’s lighter than the rest of the album.
s.src: Free Press Music: Take five with Delta Spirit (Kelly Winrich interview, 2008)
s.q: It evolved from jam that only included myself on bass, Matt on piano, and a friend/non-band member Al Kweskin on drums. So the fact that it was only a partial group of the band may have been the reason the song was created in such a lighter mood.

s.t: Delta Spirit recorded it with the rest of Ode to Sunshine in about two weeks at a friend’s cabin: mostly live, with lots of late nights and lots of wine.
s.src: NPR Weekend Edition: Delta Spirit's 'Ode To Sunshine' (transcript, 29 November 2008)
s.q: our buddy, Derek, had a cabin and a dog named Spot ... So it was about two weeks. We just recorded everything. Mostly live, few overdubs and lots of late nights, lots of wine and lots of lovin'.

s.t: Delta Spirit used an actual trash can lid as percussion on ‘Trashcan’, the hit that lifted them from local rock band to radio sensation.
s.src: LAist: Interview: Jon Jameson of the Delta Spirit
s.q: Their hit Trashcan in which they use an actual trashcan lid as percussion launched them from local rock band to radio sensation last year.

f.t: Their name comes from a shop run by bassist Jon Jameson’s great-uncle Red: the Delta Spirit Taxidermy Station of North Central Alabama. Jameson never met him.
f.src: LAist: Interview: Jon Jameson of the Delta Spirit
f.q: My mom’s Uncle Red, who was from Birmingham, AL. He had a taxidermy shop. He was an air force controller, who also ran a shop called, "Delta Spirit Taxidermy Station of North Central Alabama." So I just took Delta Spirit from that. No, I never even met Uncle Red.

f.t: Brandon Young heard Matthew Vasquez singing at 2am while buying cigarettes; four years later Young called, and within 30 minutes Vasquez had scrapped his solo record and fired his band.
f.src: NPR Weekend Edition: Delta Spirit's 'Ode To Sunshine' (transcript, 29 November 2008)
f.q: I went across the street about two o'clock in the morning to a convenience store to buy a pack of smokes, and I heard this incredible loud guy singing ... He said, the record I've been working on for six months I just threw away and fired my whole band

f.t: They sold 6,000 copies of their self-made debut album, Ode to Sunshine, mainly on the road, before Rounder Records signed them and re-released it.
f.src: American Songwriter: Three Years Of History On Delta Spirit’s History From Below
f.q: They sold 6,000 copies, mainly on the road, before catching the attention of Rounder Records, who signed the band and re-released the album.

f.t: For their second album, History from Below, they went to the studio in Cotati, California, where Tom Waits recorded all of Mule Variations.
f.src: American Songwriter: Three Years Of History On Delta Spirit’s History From Below
f.q: To record their next album, History From Below, the band went to Cotati, California, and spent time in the studio where Tom Waits recorded all of Mule Variations.

f.t: The reissued cover of their debut, Ode to Sunshine, shows a band member’s uncle, Dr Thomas Payne, raising a toast at a scientific convention on bark beetles.
f.src: ABC7 Chicago: Tuned In to Delta Spirit
f.q: the new cover is much warmer, with the smiling face of Dr. Thomas Payne (an uncle of one of the band members) raising a toast while at a scientific convention on bark beetles.
